name: drift
description: Find which dependency upgrades affect your code, see the evidence, and prepare reviewable fixes with deterministic transforms, community recipes, or your existing AI agent.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Drift runs git commands and can invoke local AI agent binaries, so it requires a trusted workspace.

commands.title: Push the Fix Branch and Open a Pull Request
Keep All Changes in This File
Undo All Changes in This File
Open Diff for a Changed File

walkthroughs.title: Ship a Safe Dependency Upgrade
walkthroughs.description: Follow Drift from dependency scan to evidence, fix, review, and release.

steps.title: Scan Dependencies
steps.description: Scan every direct dependency for an available upgrade, and see which ones would affect your code.

steps.title: Read the Evidence
steps.description: Open the report to see which upstream changes matter to this codebase.

steps.title: Fix the Affected Code
steps.description: Drift uses a deterministic transform first, an enabled community recipe second, and your selected AI agent only for what remains.

steps.title: Review Keep or Undo
steps.description: Use editor CodeLens actions and lightbulbs to keep or undo each proposed hunk.

steps.title: Ship the Branch
steps.description: Push the reviewed fix branch. Drift opens the pull request with the GitHub CLI when you have one signed in, and falls back to GitHub's own pull request page when you do not.

drift.agent.preferred.markdownDescription:
Which AI agent fixes your code. Drift drives an agent **you already have** and never asks for an API key.

Set from the Drift panel: **+ → Model**. `auto` uses the best available.

Known ids: `copilot-lm`, `copilot-cloud`, `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `aider`, `opencode`, `ollama`, and `lm:<vendor>` for any other chat-model provider registered in your editor — Drift discovers those, so the list is not fixed.

drift.agent.models.markdownDescription:
The model chosen inside each subscription, keyed by agent id — for example `{ "claude": "opus" }`.

Set from the subscription buttons in the Drift panel. A subscription with no entry uses whatever model it picks by default.

enumDescriptions: Drift may edit your files through your AI agent
Drift only analyses and explains; it never edits
drift.session.mode.markdownDescription: Set from the picker in the Drift panel. **Ask** analyses and explains. **Agent** lets your AI agent edit code.

drift.agent.efforts.markdownDescription:
How hard each subscription's model is asked to think, keyed by agent id — for example `{ "claude": "xhigh" }`.

Set from the effort dial in the Drift panel, where each level carries the name its own vendor uses: Claude runs `low`–`high` and `xhigh` (**Ultracode**), Codex runs `low`–`high` and `xhigh` (**Extra High**). Agents whose API has no reasoning budget — the in-editor Copilot models, Ollama — have no dial.

This only changes the reasoning spent on each fix. It never changes which dependencies Drift checks or which fixes it attempts — see `#drift.analysis.includeDev#` and `#drift.analysis.includePatch#` for that.

enumDescriptions: Ask in the panel before editing each group of files
Edit files, then wait for you to keep or undo each change
Edit files and commit each group without stopping
drift.session.permission.markdownDescription:
Set from the picker in the Drift panel. How much your AI agent may do unsupervised.

On the default, **Edit, then review**, nothing is ever committed until you keep it.

drift.agent.copilotModelFamily.markdownDescription: Optional model family for the in-editor Copilot agent (for example `gpt-4o`). Leave blank to let VS Code choose.

drift.agent.ollamaHost.description: Where your Ollama server is listening.

drift.agent.ollamaModel.description: Which Ollama model to use. A coding-tuned model works far better here than a general one.

drift.agent.timeoutSeconds.description: How long to let an agent work on a single commit before giving up.

drift.analysis.runOnStartup.markdownDescription: Check for breaking changes when a folder opens. Drift stays silent unless it finds something.

drift.analysis.includePatch.markdownDescription: Analyse patch bumps too. Breakage there is usually accidental, but it does happen — around 5% of npm packages have been broken by a minor or patch release.

drift.analysis.includeDev.description: Analyse dev, optional, and peer dependencies alongside runtime ones. Superseded by drift.analysis.dependencyScope once that is explicitly set; kept for anyone who already configured this.

enumDescriptions: Scan production dependencies only. Faster.
Also scan development dependencies. More complete, but can take longer.
Ask each time a scan starts.
drift.analysis.dependencyScope.markdownDescription: Which dependencies a scan looks at — the same `runtime`/`runtime+dev` choice as this Action's `dependency-scope` input. **Ask** is the default for a new install; set this explicitly to stop being asked. If you already set `#drift.analysis.includeDev#` yourself, that keeps working until you set this too — it is not read once this is.

enumDescriptions: Static analysis only. Fastest.
Also installs the upgrade and runs project checks. Much slower.
Ask each time a scan starts.
drift.analysis.verifyMode.markdownDescription: Whether a scan stops at static analysis (**quick**) or goes on to install each candidate and run this project's own checks (**deep**) — the same two modes as this Action's `verify-mode` input and the CLI's `--verify` flag. **Ask** is the default for a new install. Quick never installs anything, runs a build, or runs tests, regardless of this setting; Deep is what adds it.

drift.analysis.concurrency.markdownDescription: How many packages to check at once. **0 (the default) sizes this from your machine** — its core count and its memory — which is almost always the right answer. Checking one package is mostly waiting on the network, so raising this shortens a scan roughly in proportion, up to the point where the GitHub API starts rate-limiting and evidence turns into 'could not check'.

drift.analysis.includeTransitive.description: Analyse lockfile-only changes you did not ask for. Noisy, and rarely actionable.

drift.analysis.ignore.markdownDescription: Package name patterns to never analyse, for example `@types/*`. Added to any `ignore` list in `.github/drift.yml`.

drift.tools.autoInstall.markdownDescription: Install a missing helper analyzer (`cargo-public-api`, `japicmp`) as soon as a scan needs it, instead of asking first and requiring a second scan afterward. Turn off if you don't want Drift installing binaries globally via `cargo`/`brew` on its own.

drift.ui.showInlineDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Flag affected lines in the editor and the Problems panel, with the upstream change that caused each one.

drift.ui.showManifestCodeLens.markdownDescription: Show Drift CodeLens prompts above dependency manifests. Turn this off when the dependency tree and report are enough.

drift.fix.customInstructions.markdownDescription:
Repository conventions passed to every agent. The highest-leverage setting for output quality.

For example: *"This repo uses Vitest, not Jest. Prefer named exports. All HTTP goes through src/lib/http.ts."*

drift.fix.maxAgents.markdownDescription:
How many agents may work at once. **1** runs one commit group at a time.

Above 1, each agent gets its own `git worktree` — a private checkout of the same commit — so two agents can never overwrite each other's edits. Only groups with no file in common run together; the rest still run in order. Results are applied to your working tree in plan order, not in the order agents finish, so the review queue looks the same either way.

Stays at 1 regardless when the agent permission is **Ask before editing** (approval prompts arriving at once is not approval), for cloud agents, and where git cannot create a worktree.

drift.pullRequest.enabled.markdownDescription:
Raise a pull request once a branch is pushed.

Drift opens it directly through the GitHub CLI when you have `gh` installed and signed in, and otherwise opens GitHub's own pull request page for the branch. `gh` is a shortcut, never a requirement — the branch is pushed either way.

Drift never merges. Its output is always something a human opens, never something that has already landed.

enumDescriptions: Propose a title you can edit before the pull request is opened
Use the proposed title as-is
drift.pullRequest.confirm.markdownDescription:
Whether to confirm the pull request title first.

A proposed name you can change beats a good one you cannot — but once you trust the shape of them, **never** removes a keystroke from every upgrade.

enumDescriptions: The branch this work was started from, per git's reflog
Always the repository's default branch
drift.pullRequest.base.markdownDescription:
Which branch a pull request merges into.

**branched-from** reads git's own record of where the branch came from. On a team that develops on `develop` and releases from `main`, targeting the default branch proposes merging into the wrong place and shows a diff full of other people's commits.

When git cannot answer — a pruned reflog, a branch created before Drift ran — Drift falls back to the default branch and says so rather than guessing silently.

drift.pullRequest.draft.markdownDescription: Open pull requests as drafts, for a human to promote.

drift.pullRequest.titleTemplate.markdownDescription:
Title for pull requests Drift opens.

Placeholders: `{summary}`, `{name}`, `{from}`, `{to}`, `{count}`, `{date}`. An unrecognised placeholder is left visible rather than blanked — an obviously wrong title gets fixed, a plausible empty one does not.

drift.git.coAuthor.markdownDescription:
Add `Co-authored-by: Drift` to commits Drift makes.

You stay the author: you chose the upgrade and reviewed the diff. Turn this off if your repository lints commit trailers.

drift.git.branchPrefix.markdownDescription:
Prefix for branches Drift creates, so a team can keep its own naming convention — `drift` gives `drift/upgrade-react-18.3.1-to-19.2.0`.

When a fix starts by installing an upgrade, Drift commits those dependency files first. It never force-pushes, never rewrites history, and never commits a file an upgrade did not change.

enumDescriptions: Put every fix on a new branch, so leaving is a checkout
Edit the branch you are already on
drift.git.branchMode.markdownDescription:
Set from the git picker in the Drift panel. Where a fix does its work.

The default, **New branch**, is what makes a fix cheap to abandon: nothing an agent did can touch the branch you were on, and undoing the whole run is `git checkout -`.

enumDescriptions: Hold every change for you to keep or undo before it is committed
Commit each group as soon as the agent finishes it
drift.git.commitMode.markdownDescription:
Set from the git picker in the Drift panel. Whether Drift commits on its own.

On the default, **Ask me first**, nothing enters git history until you keep it.

enumDescriptions: File a GitHub issue
Create a local branch
File an issue and create a branch, linked together
drift.issueCreation.default.markdownDescription:
What the one-click action button on a breaking change does. The other two are always one click away in the button's dropdown.

Shared with the CLI's own `issueCreation.default` config field, so both surfaces offer the same default.

enumDescriptions: One action bundles every breaking change for a package
One action per individual breaking change
drift.issueCreation.granularity.markdownDescription: What one issue/branch covers. **Per package** (the default) is offered on each package's group header; **per change** is offered on each individual finding regardless of this setting.

drift.logLevel.description: How much Drift writes to its output channel.

drift.agent.fast.markdownDescription:
Set from the composer in the Drift panel. Which agents should trade tokens for a faster answer.

Keyed by agent id, because fast mode is a property of one subscription: Codex exposes it as a feature flag Drift can set per run, while Claude Code's `/fast` is an interactive toggle stored in its own settings — Drift inherits that one rather than overriding it.

Same model either way; only the latency and the cost change.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
scripts.package:local: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx --yes @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies --out drift.vsix && code --install-extension ./drift.vsix --force
